newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended narrowly mixed on Thursday in moderate trade on retail and interbank interest, dealers said.

"Government securities were narrowly mixed today amid uncertainty over the near-term direction of the market. Treasury bill yields were slightly lower but bond prices were slightly higher. The interbank rate was unchanged from Wednesday and volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 2.27/2.22 percent compared with Wednesday's yield of 2.35/2.30 percent.
One-year closed at a yield of 2.46/2.41 percent against Wednesday's 2.53/2.48 percent.
Among bonds, July 1998 ended at S$97.89/97.94 from Wednesday's close of S$97.88/97.93, September 2001 at S$96.57/96.62 versus S$96.52/96.57 and June 2003 at S$94.60/94.65 against S$94.50/94.55.
The overnight interbank offered rate was unchanged from Wednesday's 3-7/16 3-5/16 percent.
